name: Addis Energy
description: Addis harnesses natural geologic processes to produce ammonia at lower cost and with lower emissions. Its approach accelerates subterranean reactions to enable modular, scalable, and decentralized chemical manufacturing.

name: Adiabatic Materials
description: Adiabatic Materials produces pharmaceuticals and industrial chemicals using electricity instead of fossil-based heat. Its platform runs reactions selectively at room temperature, yielding the target product at high purity with far less waste and few byproducts — and bringing supply chains for essential medicines and fine chemicals back onshore.

name: Aepnus
description: Aepnus is developing an electrochemical platform to produce lithium salts and other industrial chemicals cost-competitively through electrified processes. The technology replaces fossil-driven production with modular, scalable routes designed for batteries and heavy industry.

name: Allie AI
description: Allie integrates data across machines, sensors, and factory systems to make operations observable and controllable. Its AI-powered analytics and agents detect anomalies, automate workflows, and optimize throughput, efficiency, and cost.

name: Alta
description: Alta uses engineered proteins to extract rare earth elements and other critical minerals from e-waste, tailings, and ores. Its biologically mediated separation systems operate under mild conditions and can refine materials below the cost of conventional processes, reshaping where and how critical minerals are sourced.

name: Andes
description: Andes helps farmers improve their farms’ efficiency and improve soil quality. By engineering microbes that fix carbon in soils, Andes lowers input costs and emissions while turning cropland into a durable carbon sink.

name: ANNEA
description: ANNEA helps renewable operators get more electricity out of existing assets. Starting with wind, its software anticipates predictable failures and applies automated control and maintenance actions to reduce downtime and increase energy output.

name: Anthro
description: Anthro develops batteries that expand the frontiers of whats possible in energy storage. Anthro’s batteries can be flexible, fire-resistant, and ultra energy-dense. Its technology enables batteries to be integrated into new form factors and environments without sacrificing safety, cost, or performance.

name: Arbor
description: Arbor produces clean baseload electricity with cost-competitive, modular gas turbines systems. Arbor’s systems can deploy faster and cheaper than any other baseload power solution, bringing a new era of scalable clean firm power to data centers, industrial customers and the grid.

name: Astro Mechanica
description: Astro Mechanica builds adaptive turboelectric propulsion systems that enable efficient, low-emissions supersonic flight. Paired with sustainable fuels, its technology reimagines aerospace propulsion for speed and sustainability.

name: Atlas Materials
description: Atlas produces high-purity nickel for battery applications through an integrated refining process that also yields low-carbon silica and high purity magnesium, which can be converted to magnesium metal. By co-producing multiple critical materials in a single system, Atlas aligns battery supply with lower cost, lower emissions, and industrial scale.

name: Cache Energy
description: Cache Energy stores excess renewable electricity as heat using a reversible solid-state chemical reaction. The result is low-cost, long-duration thermal storage that can deliver on-demand heat for homes and industrial processes without complex infrastructure.

name: CarbonChain
description: CarbonChain provides real-time emissions accounting across commodities and manufacturing supply chains. Its platform gives enterprises asset-level and cargo-specific carbon data, meeting rising demands from regulators, customers, and markets for transparent decarbonization.

name: Conifer
description: Conifer builds axial flux motors using ferrite magnets and a proprietary winding technique. The result: higher power density, lower cost, and scalable motor performance across mobility, robotics, and industrial automation – without dependence on rare earths.

name: Copper
description: Copper integrates batteries directly into appliances, offering load-shifting, backup power, and simplified electrification. Its product reduces the infrastructure required for home electrification while strengthening the grid edge.

name: ElectricFish
description: ElectricFish builds modular storage and charging systems that can be deployed without major grid upgrades. This technology enables the rapid deployment of EV charging in underserved areas, with integrated software to balance load and deliver uptime.

name: Electroflow
description: Electroflow converts lithium-rich brines into LFP cathode material in three steps, bypassing lithium carbonate and foreign processing. Its electrochemical process unlocks stranded lithium sources and delivers battery-grade material at lower cost and higher efficiency.

name: ENAPI
description: ENAPI connects the financial, technical, and operational layers of public EV charging. Its software coordinates data flows across market participants, enabling reliable interoperability and a frictionless charging experience for drivers.

name: Endurance Energy
description: Endurance produces clean baseload electricity from subsea geothermal resources, integrating drilling, generation, and power offtake into a single deployable seafloor unit. Its systems unlock a previously untapped source of firm, zero-emissions power at gigawatt scale, sized for data centers, industrial customers, and the grid.

name: Ento Labs
description: Ento uses software to optimize energy performance in commercial buildings by analyzing existing sensor and equipment data. The platform detects inefficiencies, recommends operational changes, and supports large-scale decarbonization through smarter load management and reduced waste.

name: Foundation Alloy
description: Foundation Alloy produces engineering alloys through MetalsFIRST, a solid-state manufacturing platform that builds high-performance metals without melting. The process unlocks compositions and properties legacy methods can't reach, with fewer processing steps and significantly higher strength than commercial alternatives.

name: Generate
description: Generate’s tools help architects and developers rapidly evaluate viable mass timber designs using real material inventories and engineering constraints. By shortening early design cycles and simplifying manufacturing alignment, Generate accelerates the development of high-performance prefabricated building systems.

name: InRange
description: InRange creates localized energy marketplaces that connect landowners, developers, and electricity buyers. Its end-to-end platform handles development, interconnection, and sales, unlocking distributed generation where grid capacity is limited.

name: Intensivate
description: Intensivate’s parallel processor chip architecture improves power efficiency and throughput for data-intensive workloads. Designed to integrate seamlessly into data centers, its chip addresses rising compute demand while cutting operating costs and energy consumption at scale.

name: Leeta Materials
description: Leeta’s microwave-based furnace system enables the production of alloys at higher quallity than otherwise possible, and with lower energy use. By integrating automation and analytics, Leeta ensures consistent output quality and cost efficiency for materials used in semiconductors, electronics, and advanced alloys.

name: Limelight Steel
description: Limelight uses light to reduce iron ore, eliminating the need for carbon-based reductants and avoiding associated emissions. Its process enables cost-competitive, lower-carbon steelmaking using abundant low-grade ores, with lower capital requirements than traditional furnaces.

name: Lydian
description: Lydian converts CO₂ and water into fuels and chemical feedstocks through a thermochemical process designed for carbon-neutral production. The system supports drop-in replacements across aviation and industrial chemistry without reliance on biomass or fossil hydrocarbons.

name: Mitti Labs
description: Mitti combines remote sensing, IoT, and ground validation to measure and reduce methane emissions from rice farming. These tools help growers implement more efficient practices, verify reductions, and access new revenue from carbon markets – aligning emissions goals with farm profitability.

name: Moment Energy
description: Moment Energy creates energy storage systems from repurposed EV batteries. By combining refurbished packs with proprietary battery management software, Moment extends system life and delivers lower-cost storage for commercial and utility-scale customers while advancing a more circular battery supply chain.

name: NewOrbit
description: NewOrbit builds satellites engineered to operate in Very Low Earth Orbit, the band 200 to 300 km above Earth that has remained beyond commercial reach. By flying three times closer to Earth than conventional satellites, its spacecraft deliver higher-resolution imagery, faster data, direct-to-device connectivity, and live HD video at a fraction of the cost of existing systems.

name: Photara
description: Photora develops laser-based metallization tools and consumables that replace silver in solar cells with base metals. This reduces raw material cost, simplifies supply chains, and supports expansion of PV production with fewer constraints on critical materials.

name: Powerline
description: Powerline is the control layer for an increasingly complex grid. It ingests telemetry from storage, generation, and transmission assets, applies predictive models, and sends intelligent signals to optimize performance. This is cleaner, smarter power without downtime.

name: Remora
description: Remora captures CO₂ directly from emitting machines like trains and trucks and monetizes it through commodity markets. This allows fleets to decarbonize without overhauling vehicles or waiting for new drivetrain technology, while turning pollution into profit.

name: SirenOpt
description: SirenOpt uses cold plasma sensors and ML to detect nanometer-scale defects in battery and semiconductor production. Its platform improves yields, lowers scrap rates, and shortens time to revenue in high-value manufacturing lines.

name: Skyven Technologies
description: Skyven provides electrified heat-as-a-service for industrial facilities, replacing fossil boilers with high-efficiency heat pumps. Its platform combines system design, financing, and controls, enabling rapid deployment of zero-emissions steam.

name: SnoFox
description: SnowFox uses physical modeling and sensor data to simulate and optimize thermal flows in refrigerated warehouses and cold chain facilities. This reduces energy consumption and improves layout and equipment decisions in a sector historically overlooked in decarbonization efforts.

name: Spore.Bio
description: Spore.Bio uses multimodal photonics hardware and a transformer-based AI model to replace legacy technology for bacterial detection. The hardware reads the unique spectral fingerprint of microorganisms driving rapid detection, identification, and quantification for food and beverage, pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and clinical applications.

name: Stealth

name: tem
description: tem redesigns how power is priced and contracted, replacing opaque legacy intermediaries with AI that delivers clearer pricing and structurally lower costs. By aligning energy prices more closely with the underlying cost of generation, tem helps businesses pay less and generators earn more.

description: KOKO builds and deploys dense networks of cloud-connected "KOKOpoints" inside local corner stores, which serve as consumer access points for goods and services delivered in partnership with major suppliers. The first consumer solution is a liquid ethanol cooking fuel, which delivers significant cost savings and quality of life improvements in the multi-billion dollar market for urban cooking fuel in Africa.

name: LETA
description: Leta is an AI-driven logistics optimization platform that connects to a company’s existing ERP/ordering systems and automatically plans the most efficient loads, routes, and delivery schedules. Its software gives dispatchers real-time visibility, driver tracking, and performance analytics, helping businesses cut fleet costs, reduce failed deliveries, and move more goods with fewer vehicles. The result for clients is materially lower logistics spend, higher delivery reliability, and a scalable, data-driven supply-chain operation.

name: Metro Africa Xpress (MAX.NG)
description: MAX.NG provides solution for mobility challenges in Africa. Any driver or owner of commercial transport now has an access to financing for the expansion of the fleet, insurance, a trip accounting system, a payment platform, and convenient service for obtaining all documentation. Max.ng also provides a transition to electric transport decreasing CO2 emissions.

name: OCTONIC VR
description: Octonic VR workout makes treadmill training fun, safe and requires minimum investment in time and effort. With realistic visuals, interactive virtual reality worlds, and real or AI runners in the game, the users can compete and explore the best routes on our planet. Walking and running using Octonic’s proprietary VR technology prevents motion sickness and is as safe as using a conventional treadmill.

name: SABI
description: Sabi is Africa’s leading provider of digital infrastructure powering the sourcing and distribution of critical commodities to domestic and international markets Africa’s small-scale producers and traders don’t have a structured route to market for their commodities, hindering the ability for their supply to contribute to global demand Sabi's innovative platform seamlessly integrates advanced tools and services, simplifying both domestic and cross-border supply chain transactions and facilitating trade through increased market accessibility and transparency.

name: SkillCampVR
description: SkillCampVR empowers enterprises with immersive, on-demand VR training that replaces slide-based instruction with realistic scenarios tailored to regulated industries (e.g., security, aviation, facilities management). Their platform enables anytime, anywhere access to modules built to industry standards, driving faster up-skilling, stronger compliance, and measurable reductions in training cost and risk.

description: A revolutionary technology, printing electrodes on solar panels. The new method eliminates defects, increases efficiency of PV Cell by 4–5%, and significantly decreases production costs.

name: XPLENTY

name: ZEROAVIA

name: ANAPHITE
description: Anaphite offers an industry-leading solution to the challenges of dry coating cathodes with its chemical compositing process to make dry coating precursor powders. The patented technology has the potential to make EV battery manufacturing 30% less carbon intensive and 40% cheaper, and the UK-based company is already working with global car and battery cell manufacturers. Anaphite has patented chemistry-based battery electrode production technology that reduces the cost of EV batteries by 5-10% - independent of the battery chemistry. The company has already proven the technology’s capability in lithium-ion battery production, and it will also be applicable to a wide range of new battery technologies, including sodium-ion and solid state. The team’s exceptionally pragmatic and future-focused mindset is another key asset. Alex and Sam brought in Joe Stevenson as CEO in 2022 when they were looking to scale and reach customers. Joe is an experienced commercial lead at the helm of the company, and has helped Anaphite progress to the next level. This type of foresight is absolutely essential when creating new technology companies, where’s the next gap and how to fill it, and puts them in the best position to scale quickly. The scale of Anaphite’s ambition and potential is also clearly reflected in the consortium of the Series A. We’re experienced investors based all around the world, from our round co-leads Maniv in the US/Israel, to EEI in Japan, and Nesta in the UK. We all believe this company has what it takes to win across geographies. This company is setting new standards for battery production and can help us reach a decarbonised future faster and more efficiently. We're looking forward to helping Anaphite’s technology go global and reduce the costs of the entire battery industry to the benefit of all. Website: Anaphite Founded 2018 Management Alexander Hewitt, Co-Founder Samuel Burrow, CTO Joe Stevenson, CEO Location Bristol, UK Segment Energy World Fund Investment Stage

name: Barocal
description: Barocal is replacing harmful refrigerants with high-efficiency solid-state cooling technology for the $500B global HVAC market. Cambridge-based Barocal is commercialising solid-state cooling using barocaloric materials, a breakthrough resulting from 15 years of research at the University of Cambridge. Instead of cycling high-GWP refrigerant gases like conventional systems, Barocal’s technology applies pressure to proprietary solid-state barocaloric materials to transfer heat. This eliminates refrigerant leakage and the emissions associated with it. Why we invested in Barocal The climate case : Cooling emits over 4 Gt CO₂e annually, accounting for more than 7% of global greenhouse gas emissions, which makes it one of the largest decarbonisation blind spots. These emissions come from HFC refrigerant leakage, which often have global warming potentials more than 1,000 times higher than CO₂, as well as from the energy intensity of cooling itself. Cooling demand is projected to triple by 2050 , further increasing these emissions. Barocal directly addresses both leakage and energy consumption by eliminating refrigerant gases entirely and delivering significantly higher efficiency than existing solutions. The business case : The global HVAC market is worth approximately $450 billion and is expected to grow to $577 billion by 2033. Barocal is initially focused on commercial chillers and data centre cooling, targeting some of the fastest-growing and most profitable segments. The company is working in collaboration with large OEMs to bring the technology to market. In addition to the emissions benefits, higher efficiency reduces energy costs and results in a lower total cost of ownership for customers. The team : Prof. Xavier Moya, Co-Founder and CEO, is a Professor of Materials Physics at the University of Cambridge and a globally recognised pioneer in caloric materials and barocalorics. He has authored more than 150 scientific publications with over 15,000 citations. He founded Barocal to commercialise his breakthrough research, funded by the Royal Society and the European Research Council. Dr. Giles Rodway, Co-Founder and CTO, brings decades of industrial R&D experience from the automotive sector and previously founded Spinetic, combining deep engineering expertise with proven entrepreneurial credibility. Website: https://barocal.com/ Founded 2019 Management Prof. Xavier Moya Dr. Giles Rodway Location Cambridge, UK Segment Industry World Fund Investment Stage

name: ECOWORKS
description: ECOWORKS IS A SERIAL RENOVATION SOLUTION PROVIDER. The company offers a swift automated estimate, detailed planning, seamless construction and installation of a refurbishment project. Their serial renovation approach brings industrial manufacturing methods to the construction industry. The unique solution enables faster net-zero renovation with lower costs, less labour and higher quality at the same time. Why we invested: The climate case : Today, around 75% of buildings in Europe are considered energy inefficient, and over half of the continent's 315 million residential units have energy performance ratings of E or worse. Thus, in Germany alone, buildings account for 35% of total energy consumption. This situation is preventing European countries from meeting their built environment climate targets. The business case : ecoworks’ AI-driven 3D planning solution and scalable modular construction is primed to benefit from regulatory demands for renovation of existing buildings. Their retrofits are quicker (15 vs 26-40 weeks) and to a higher energy efficiency rating than the market average. Therefore, their solution is increasing property values and helping residents save on energy bills, all without requiring tenants to leave their homes. The team : Ecoworks’ founder and CEO, Emanuel Heisenberg, is an inspiring serial entrepreneur, author and policy advisor with an established track record in the climate tech and energy space. He has managed to build a team with high-level, professional expertise in pre-fab construction and procurement, and experience scaling within the real estate sector. name: Enerkii
description: enerkii is slashing industrial energy bills while decarbonising one of Europe’s hardest-to-abate sectors. The Munich-based company provides a full-service, emissions-free energy system for industrial and commercial players across Europe. By combining software intelligence with on-site renewable infrastructure, enerkii enables companies to cut their energy bills by up to 50%, with zero upfront investment. Through its unique “Energy-as-a-Service” model, enerkii is eliminating the complexity, risk, and cost of industrial decarbonisation. Why we invested in enerkii The climate case: Energy production accounts for ~75% of global CO₂ emissions, and industrial energy use remains one of the slowest sectors to decarbonise. Over 80% of industrial sites in Germany still rely on fossil fuels despite increasing renewable availability. enerkii directly addresses this by enabling affordable, zero-emission on-site energy generation. With 87 MW of contracted capacity already secured, enerkii is on track to reduce industrial emissions at scale - just as Germany and the EU accelerate towards 2030 renewable energy targets. The business case: enerkii unlocks an enormous untapped market: the decarbonisation of Europe’s commercial and industrial sectors. While competitors focus on point solutions, enerkii offers a fully integrated system, including solar, battery storage, charging infrastructure, and (soon) heat pumps. These assets are backed by a proprietary Operating System (OS) that configures optimal setups in minutes. Their business model is elegant and compelling: no investment, no complexity, just savings. enerkii already has 18 contracts with major German industrial players, and is well-positioned for Europe-wide expansion. The team: Co-founder and CEO David Balensiefen is a serial entrepreneur who previously co-founded gridX, which he successfully exited to E.ON. He is joined by gridX veterans Henry Thierhoff and Hendrik Abel, forming a team with deep technical knowledge, proven operational execution, and a bold vision for building Europe’s next major decentralised energy provider. The business case: ENOUGH has the ingredients to become the global leader in sustainable protein. It is tackling crucial bottlenecks in its production and provides supply security to a growing market. In addition, products featuring ABUNDA win over customers for taste, emulating the texture and taste of traditional meat. name: FARMLESS
description: FARMLESS CREATES CARBON NEGATIVE, FUNCTIONAL PROTEINS THAT CUT OUT THE NEED FOR AGRICULTURAL LAND. The Farmless process combines the ancient craft of fermentation – which has been used for millennia to brew beer and bake bread – with a modern feedstock, the scientific term for a starter liquid. Why we invested: The climate case: Whereas most fermentation companies rely on sugar, Farmless uses a feedstock made from CO2, water, nitrogen and renewable energy – bypassing the need for agricultural land. This is a major breakthrough. Agriculture has taken over almost half of all habitable land on earth, pushing nature over the brink, and the world needs an affordable protein source that can be produced without excessive land use. The business case: the demand for meat and dairy is set to soar with a growing population, and we need dramatically more efficient, scalable ways of protein production - fast. Farmless’ technology will help scale alternative proteins which meet long-term, buoyant consumer demand. The team: the Farmless team, led by Adnan Oner, combines physicists, food experts, communications leaders and data analysts who will drive the start-up forward in the coming years. name: Hyperscale Power
description: HYPERSCALE POWER IS BUILDING THE NEXT GENERATION OF ELECTRIC POWER INFRASTRUCTURE. The Zurich-based deeptech company is developing compact solid-state transformers (SSTs) designed for the power demands of AI data centres, EV charging, and large-scale renewable energy systems. Hyperscale Power’s proprietary design is roughly 10× smaller than conventional transformers and uses around 90% less material, dramatically reducing deployment timelines from years to weeks. By leveraging high-frequency operation and advanced power electronics, the system achieves energy-conversion efficiencies of up to 98.5% – significantly higher than today’s solutions. With a clear efficiency, cost, and emissions advantage, Hyperscale Power is positioned to unlock faster electrification and power delivery for the infrastructure underpinning the next industrial era. Why we invested in Hyperscale Power The climate case: Electricity systems lose around 6–8% of generated power globally through transmission and conversion inefficiencies. At the same time, the rapid growth of AI compute, EV charging networks, and renewable power generation is dramatically increasing electricity demand. Hyperscale Power’s solid-state transformers offer up to 98.5% energy-conversion efficiency and enable more flexible, modular grid architectures that can integrate renewables more effectively. Even a 2% improvement in efficiency at hyperscale data-centre and grid level translates into millions of tonnes of avoided CO₂ emissions. The company’s compact design also reduces material usage by roughly 90%, lowering embodied emissions and supporting a more resource-efficient power infrastructure. The business case: Hyperscale Power is entering a rapidly expanding multi-billion-euro market driven by hyperscalers, electrification, and global investment in energy infrastructure. Transformer supply chains are currently strained, with lead times stretching to 18–24 months as demand for high-power systems accelerates. Hyperscale Power’s SST technology dramatically shortens deployment timelines while delivering higher efficiency and power density. This creates a compelling value proposition for data centres, EV charging networks, and renewable-energy operators that need faster, more efficient power conversion to meet growing electricity demands. The team: Hyperscale Power was founded in 2025 by Daniel Rothmund and Sami Pettersson, who each bring more than a decade of experience in solid-state transformers and medium-voltage high-power converters. Their deep technical expertise in power electronics and transformer architecture underpins the company’s proprietary design. Based in Zurich, the team benefits from close ties to Europe’s leading engineering ecosystem around ETH Zürich, positioning the company to attract top technical talent and rapidly bring its technology to market. Website: Hyperscale Power Founded 2025 Management Daniel Rothmund, CEO Sami Pettersson, CTO Location Zürich, Switzerland Segment Energy World Fund Investment Stage

name: JUICY MARBLES
description: Juicy Marbles is a plant-based protein food tech startup that developed one of the world’s first plant-based whole cuts in 2019. The Slovenian company has accurately recreated the texture and taste of cuts of filet mignon and recently released products across Europe to great acclaim. Juicy Marbles steaks are currently on sale at 500 stores across the continent. Why we invested: The climate case: Animal agriculture is one of the largest GHG-emitting industries and is hugely inefficient - wasting caloric energy, water, and land resources. It has been the primary driver of deforestation and a catalyst for desertification in the Amazon. There are numerous ground beef alternatives on the market, but ground beef only contributes 40% of emissions from this livestock category. This is where Juicy Marbles’ whole cuts come in. The business case: Juicy Marble’s filet mignon pioneers the plant-based market. They are creating a product closer to the texture, fat profile and taste of a traditional beef steak. Their focus on manufacturing whole cut-resembling products, enhanced by strong branding and educational resources, has helped them build up a cult following and international commercial success. The team: CEO Tilen Travnik trained as a biotechnologist, before founding D:Labs - an incubator that helped internet startups launch and scale. CBO Vladimir Mićković has co-founded numerous branding agencies in his native Slovenia - including Ljudje, Flaviar and KUCHA. Co-CEO Luka Sinček is a microbiologist and former founder of the Biotechnical Ecosystem of Slovenia. name: LITHOSQUARE
description: Lithosquare is accelerating critical minerals discovery with AI-driven geological intelligence that addresses the global supply bottleneck. The Paris-based company helps mining companies identify, rank and advance high-potential copper, lithium and rare earth deposits, faster, with higher confidence and at a fraction of the traditional cost. What sets Lithosquare apart is its geology-first approach. Where most AI-exploration tools look for statistical patterns in historical data, Lithosquare reasons from the science of how deposits form. Its platform is built around a proprietary metallogeny ontology covering around 20 deposit types, developed and maintained by PhD metallogenists working alongside AI engineers. This allows the system to generate credible targets in greenfield areas where no historical training data exists, a capability that pattern matching approaches cannot replicate. Why we invested in Lithosquare The climate case: Only around 1 in 1,000 mineral exploration projects ever becomes a mine, yet global demand for copper, lithium and rare earths is accelerating as electrification and AI infrastructure intensify. Average mine development lead times have stretched to nearly 18 years, creating a critical gap between exploration decisions today and production needed in the 2030s and 2040s. Lithosquare directly addresses this bottleneck by accelerating high-confidence discovery in jurisdictions that can meet Western supply-chain resilience requirements. By bringing new reserves to market faster and from jurisdictions with stronger environmental standards, Lithosquare unblocks the materials supply that global electrification depends on. The business case: Global mineral exploration budgets have historically ranged between $12-15bn annually, with a portion allocated to target generation, data analytics and technical advisory. Lithosquare's asset-light, partnership-driven model captures exploration service revenues while retaining long-term economic upside through Net Smelter Return royalties on successful discoveries. The global royalty and streaming sector has a combined enterprise value of over $140bn. Early partnerships validate strong demand for AI-accelerated exploration workflows and demonstrate traction across both large-cap operators and mid-tier explorers. The team: Co-Founder and CEO Aymeric Preveral-Etcheverry previously scaled Fieldbox, an industrial AI company. COO Simon Leclair brings 15+ years of mining expertise, including early-career mine development work at Eramet and 8 years as a partner at BCG specialising in Metals and Mining strategy. Both are Mines Paris graduates, combining deep geological credibility with proven operational execution and AI expertise. Website: https://www.lithosquare.com/ Founded 2024 Management Aymeric Preveral-Etcheverry, Co-Founder & CEO Simon Leclair, Founding COO Location Paris, France Segment Industry / Critical Materials World Fund Investment Stage

name: MISSION ZERO TECHNOLOGY
description: MISSION ZERO DEVELOPS A VERSATILE, SCALABLE DIRECT AIR CAPTURE SOLUTION (DAC) FOR GLOBAL APPLICATION. Mission Zero offers a modular electrochemical DAC solution powered by renewable electricity and built by off-the-shelf technology to deliver carbon removal at scale. Why we invested: The climate case : DAC is essential for achieving our global net-zero targets. According to the IPCC , up to 10 gigatonnes of CO2 must be removed from the atmosphere annually by 2050. DAC will enable the reversal of the temporary overshoot from historical emissions and emissions from hard-to-abate industries. The business case : Mission Zero's electrochemical DAC system is primed to overcome the current bottlenecks of affordability and scalability through significant energy savings, increased process efficiency, and a modular scale-up approach. The company is expected to achieve market-leading CO2 prices at a capacity of 1,000 tonnes of CO2 per year, facilitating a commercially feasible scale-up roadmap. The team : Mission Zero’s CEO, Nicholas Chadwick, is a Ph.D.-trained chemist and materials scientist with extensive experience in scaling hardware technologies. COO, Shiladity Ghosh, began his career in academia, earning a Ph.D. in chemical engineering at Imperial College London, and holds an additional MBA. CTO, Gaël Gobaille-Shaw, is a Ph.D.-trained electrochemist experienced in establishing world-leading IP strategies. name: NITRICITY
description: Nitricity is electrifying organic fertilizer production with a world-first, plant-based alternative that’s transforming agriculture. The US-based company has developed Ash Tea , a liquid organic nitrogen fertilizer made from recycled almond shells, air, water, and renewable energy. Fully vegan, pathogen-free, and cost-competitive, Ash Tea is already sold out for years to come, with farmers lining up to secure supply. With its first commercial-scale facility breaking ground in Delhi, California, Nitricity is scaling globally to meet surging demand from organic growers in the US and Europe. Why we invested in Nitricity The climate case: Conventional fertilizers made through the Haber-Bosch process are responsible for ~2% of global GHG emissions, while also degrading soils, polluting waterways, and driving biodiversity loss. Worse, up to 70% of nitrogen applied is lost to the environment 1 . Nitricity’s organic, circular alternative cuts emissions by more than 90% and restores soil health, while replacing animal-based fertilizers with a cleaner, safer option. By producing nitrogen fertilizer from agricultural waste and renewable energy, Nitricity directly addresses one of agriculture’s most urgent decarbonisation challenges. The business case: Nitricity is addressing the $150B global fertilizer market, starting with a beachhead in organic nitrogen fertilizer for high-value crops, a segment worth over $11B on its own 2 . Farmers are eager for better, affordable solutions, and Nitricity delivers. Its product flows seamlessly through irrigation systems, avoids clogging, and enables more efficient nitrogen use, cutting input costs. With over $150m already in its sales pipeline and binding offtake agreements stretching through 2028, Nitricity is scaling from proven demand, not speculative adoption. The company’s Series B raise, closed in the third quarter of 2025, will accelerate US expansion, advance R&D, and build the European customer pipeline and partnerships in preparation for international growth. The team: Founded in 2018 by Stanford graduates Dr. Nicolas Pinkowski (CEO), Dr. Joshua McEnaney (President & CTO), and Dr. Jay Schwalbe (CSO), Nitricity began with a solar-powered experiment on a lemon tree. Today, the founders lead a 38-person team with deep scientific expertise, a clear commercial track record, and a bold vision for circular, plant-based fertilizer production. Their entrepreneurial grit, coupled with strategic backing from leading climate and agri-tech investors, positions Nitricity as a future global leader in sustainable fertilizer. name: NZN
description: Net Zero Nitrogen (NZN) is pioneering a new generation of sustainable agriculture with its breakthrough biofertilizer solution. The UK-based agtech company is developing a novel bioinoculant using naturally occurring endophytic bacteria that colonize crops to reduce the need for synthetic nitrogen fertilizers (SNFs). Unlike most alternatives, NZN’s solution is non-GM, requires no new machinery, and is easy to apply. It offers farmers a “green discount”: lower costs with higher yields and reduced emissions. NZN has already shown strong traction in ASEAN, where it is preparing to scale with the support of major climate-focused investors. Why we invested in NZN The climate case: Synthetic nitrogen fertilizers are responsible for ~2% of global GHG emissions (1.13 Gt CO₂e) and are a leading source of nitrous oxide, a greenhouse gas nearly 300 times more potent than CO₂. The production and overuse of SNFs also damages soil microbiomes, pollutes waterways, and drives biodiversity loss. NZN’s bioinoculant technology delivers up to 88% fewer emissions during production and mitigates downstream pollution. This makes it a powerful lever for climate mitigation in agriculture, a sector often overlooked in decarbonisation. The business case: NZN is entering a $200B global fertilizer market with a solution that’s both more sustainable and more cost-effective. The product requires no regulatory exemptions, no GM approval, and no farmer behavior change. It’s already generating significant traction in ASEAN markets through multiple proof-of-concept trials and interest from major agri-input distributors. With minimal transmission loss and no nitrous oxide leakage, NZN offers not just a green premium, but a green discount. The team: CEO Justin Hughes brings entrepreneurial vision and leadership experience as a former Red Arrows pilot, while CSO Dr. Gary Devine leads scientific development with deep biological expertise. Together with co-founder Alan Burbidge, the NZN team combines scientific rigour and strategic execution, positioning the company to transform one of agriculture’s most polluting inputs. Website: NZN Founded 2022 Management Justin Hughes, CEO Gary Devine, CSO Alan Burbidge, Hd Corp Affairs Location Nottingham, United Kingdom Segment Food, Agriculture & Land Use (FALU) World Fund Investment Stage

name: PLANET A FOODS
description: Planet A Foods is a food-tech company that developed a technology platform to create a socially-just and environmentally-friendly food industry. They develop sustainable, future-oriented products free from any highly-limited resources such as cocoa or palm oil. All items are created from solely natural ingredients - with the first use case being cacao butter & cacao powder. Why we invested: The climate case : Chocolate production comes at a high cost for the planet. The rising demand for cocoa is a major driver for the deforestation in tropical forests, which are some of the most important carbon sinks on our planet. Climate change itself - and the broader biodiversity crisis - is also threatening the viability of producing cocoa. The business case : the great barrier for any food-tech business is the taste test. Planet A Foods’ Nocoa product offers a nearly identical taste and texture to conventionally produced chocolate - because of its fermentation approach - the best on the market we have tried. The team : CEO Maximilian has previously founded 27Pilots, a boutique consultancy helping startups secure venture funding. Prior he also worked in the automobile industry for half a decade. CTO Sara was a researcher at the Technical University of Munich, analysing the molecular structure of coffee, before working as Principal Scientist at Atomo Coffee, and as Head of Flavour at the Zurich University of Applied Sciences. name: Quantum Diamonds
description: QuantumDiamonds accelerates semiconductor development, improves production yields, and is poised to become the only startup to win manufacturing funding under the European Chips Act. Quantum Diamonds Sensor Technology (QDST) is redefining chip testing with world-first quantum sensing tools that detect hidden defects in complex semiconductors. The Munich-based company enables manufacturers to identify faults in 3D chip architectures before energy- and water-intensive processing steps, reducing waste and emissions. QDST’s platform provides non-destructive, nanometer-scale current imaging, pushing the boundaries of semiconductor metrology. Already working with global chip leaders, QDST is scaling manufacturing with support from the European Chips Act to meet soaring demand for high-yield, high-performance chips. The climate case: The semiconductor industry’s energy use has surged by 125% in recent years, with yield losses causing unnecessary energy, water, and material consumption. QDST’s breakthrough testing tools catch defects early, improving yields and cutting emissions by over 5% through yield optimisation. Additional emissions savings are expected from battery-yield optimisation, as well as from the indirect effects of accelerated EV adoption and enhanced computing efficiency. At scale, these combined effects will drive significant CO2 reductions across critical industries, directly supporting global decarbonisation efforts. The business case: As chips become denser and more complex, today’s tools fall short. QDST is entering a €20B market with a unique solution that solves a growing industry bottleneck. Its quantum sensing system enables accurate, fast, and non-destructive testing of advanced chips, critical for AI, HPC, and EV technologies. Already used by leading global chipmakers, QDST is now scaling production and deployments to become the new testing standard in semiconductor fabs worldwide. The team: Co-founders Kevin Berghoff, Dr. Fleming Bruckmaier, and Prof. Dr. Dominik Bucher lead a world-class team of physicists, engineers, and software developers from TUM, ETH Zurich, LMU, and Harvard. With backing from semiconductor veterans with decades of experience at ASML, Intel, TSMC, and Applied Materials, QDST combines deep technical excellence with strategic industry insight. name: SPACE FORGE
description: Space Forge is on a mission to lead the next industrial revolution by harnessing space. The UK-based startup is developing a fully returnable satellite platform designed for manufacturing superior materials in orbit to enable large-scale emissions reduction on Earth. These satellites will leverage a zero-gravity, zero-pollution production environment- with high-efficiency semiconductors as one of its first use cases Why we invested: The climate case : global IT energy use to hit 20% of global emissions by 2030. Space Forge’s in-space manufactured semiconductors can reduce energy usage by 75% - by harnessing unique space conditions of microgravity, vacuum and low temperatures. The business case : semiconductor production on earth is reaching its technological limits. In-orbit manufacturing can bring about an 88% increase in computational efficiency, as well as a 50% reduction in costs compared to production on Earth. Space Forge’s technology is highly scalable and is expected to have enough manufacturing capacity to cover 5G networks in Germany and the UK in the next 5 years. The returnable satellite platform on its own is a technology with several sizable market-changing opportunities. The team: CEO Joshua Western has worked in the space industry for over a decade. He worked closely with key government and industry stakeholders at the beginning of his career at Thales Space and later at the UK Space Agency. Co-founder and CTO Andrew Bacon is a senior expert in designing and launching satellites. Since 2009, he has been working for industry leaders like Clyde Space, SEA and Thales. name: VAERIDION
description: Munich-based aircraft manufacturer VÆRIDION is developing a zero-emission electric Microliner that is on track to deliver affordable regional flights in Europe by 2030 . VÆRIDION is the first e-aviation company to have secured a milestone Pre-Application Contract (PAC) with the EASA – a highly significant achievement that confirms VÆRIDION’s Microliner meets certification standards for commercial passenger aircraft, and puts the company ahead of competitors. Their patented prototype Microliner will start as a nine-seater aircraft. The Microliner has a nominal range of 400 km plus IFR reserves, has already passed initial functional and validation tests, and has prototype flights set to take off in 2027. The company has plans in place to scale the technology to long-term offer pan-European flights. The Microliner is a fixed-wing aircraft with advanced battery-wing integration and multi-engine single propeller configuration, all designed for maximum safety and efficiency. It emits less noise than conventional aircraft, making it well-suited to smaller airfields and easy to roll out in underserved areas. Delivered at scale, it would help drive economic growth and accessibility. Europe is currently nowhere near reaching its sustainable aviation goals, and the Microliner presents a long-term solution. VÆRIDION has already signed its first customers in Denmark (Copenhagen AirTaxi and Copenhagen Helicopter), Benelux (ASL Group) and Germany (Aero-Dienst). The Microliner will initially serve business passengers before expanding into consumer travel. The company already wields a world-class team made up of 38 aerospace, software and automotive experts, and partnerships with institutions including TU Munich and Bauhaus Luftfahrt e.V. In 2024, VÆRIDION also opened a state-of-the-art battery development facility at the Bosch Collaboration Campus and launched a Dutch subsidiary, which will allow VÆRIDION to leverage the innovation ecosystem surrounding TU Delft and accelerate the journey to commercialisation. VÆRIDION is also exploring applications for the aircraft in air ambulance services in collaboration with Aero-Dienst, which operates a fleet on behalf of ADAC. The company's technology converts sensor data into safe and low-cost map information created specifically to direct fully autonomous vehicles through artificial intelligence and vehicle-based local processing, enabling autonomous vehicles with comprehensive and precise knowledge to operate safely and smoothly on all roads.

name: Clarity Money

The company's personal finance application uses artificial intelligence and data science to help consumers to make better financial decisions and get the most from their money, enabling users to cancel and lower bills, get a better credit card, create a savings account and manage their finances.

name: Clearco

name: Climate X

The site recently expanded its class offerings to include video classes on standardized test preparation and technology training. description: Gallant is an animal health biotech company developing FDA-regulated stem cell therapies for pets.

name: Gear6
description: Acquired by Violin Systems. Provider of scalable and centralized storage caching solutions for data centers.

The company develops interactive entertainment video games and boasts a broad portfolio of pc games such as Halo, Battleborn, Half Life, Brothers in Arms and Borderlands, enabling gamers to engage in interactive content.

name: Gemfire

name: Genband
description: Acquired by Ribbon Communications. The company's communications software easily connects and rapidly deploys business and consumer services, enabling service providers, enterprises and systems integrators to weave real-time contextual communications into business and consumer applications and workflows for a productive and engaging user experience.

name: General Assembly
description: Acquired by Adecco Group. Provider of in-demand education and career services created to empower individuals to pursue work they love. The company's full-time immersive programs provide educational programming, space and support to facilitate collaborative practices and learning opportunities across the community, providing users with employment information and opportunities in technologies.

name: Genteric
description: Developer of non-viral gene therapy delivery systems to correct human disease. The company's non-viral delivery system allows a patient's gastrointestinal system to produce and secrete therapeutic proteins into the bloodstream.

name: Getable
description: Provider of online equipment rental reservation services intended to let construction professionals order and manage equipment from their smartphone. The company's platform offers customers to get the equipment they need from the suppliers at fair rates, enabling rental providers to increase the overall utilization of their assets and users to search, compare and rent equipment online from local suppliers in a hassle-free manner.

name: Giant
description: Giant is the operator of an AI digital studio for children to engage in animation and storytelling. The company's product converts images, videos, and prompts into animated products that can be edited and added to, creating a creative, AI powered workspace for children. ​

name: Gigafin Networks
description: Provider of streamlined insight, cost-effective internal security and control over traffic within the LAN. The company provides appliances which features firewall, flow monitoring, traffic management, peer-to-peer application management and denial of service prevention applications.

name: Gigaom
description: Acquired by GigaOm. Provider of online media, events and research services. The company offers analysis and research on emerging technology markets.

name: GiveForward
description: Acquired by YouCaring. Provider of an online fundraising platform designed to support users to create fundraising pages to raise money. The company's Web portal allows people to create personalized fundraising pages and share their cause through social media such as Facebook and Twitter, enabling users to raise money for chemotherapy, organ transplants, mission trips and funeral expenses.

name: Gizmo5
description: Acquired by Alphabet. Provider of voice over internet protocol service. The company provides Gizmo5 mobile and desktop software.

name: Gladly Software
description: Developer of a cloud-based communication platform designed to help businesses to deliver better customer service. The company's platform gives agents a single view of the customers across all conversations, no matter what communication channel and provides companies with real-time insight into their contact center, enabling big enterprise customers to reimagine and reinvent how customer service can be delivered.

name: Glide
description: Developer of communication platform designed to make authentic communication accessible. The company's platform provides a live video chat and messaging application for both the ios and android operating systems, providing customers with live real-time video communications.

Readers can discover and read content across various genres. The platform provides tools for creators to monetize their work through subscriptions, sales, and ad revenue sharing, serving as both a publishing platform and digital marketplace for independent and established comic creators.

name: gloStream
description: Acquired by Triarq Health. Provider of enterprise software for the healthcare sector. The company offers physicians and healthcare facilities software platforms for electronic medical records (EMRs) and practice management.

name: Gluon Networks
description: Acquired by DASAN Zhone Solutions. Manufacturer of networking products for local telephone companies. The company offers converged switching systems for telecommunications service providers. It also provides switching and signaling gateway interface that bridges next generation VoIP networks with legacy circuit switch networks.

name: GoFormz
description: Developer of an online document management platform intended to transform paper forms into mobile forms that make it easy to run reports and get data. The company's platform creates a digital version of the existing form or creates a new one from scratch, enabling businesses to make efficient decisions and save administrative costs across their team.

name: Good Counsel
description: Developer of an online menswear selling platform designed to create a community that embraces men of a larger size. The company's platform provides fashion consultation and special shopping requests in menswear for the big and tall community, empowering men to live well, dress well and do so with purpose.

name: Good Eggs
description: Operator of an online grocery delivery platform intended to delivers thoughtfully sourced fresh produce to consumers. The company provides a wide assortment of local and organic produce, sustainable meat, seafood products and grocery staples from nearby farms and local food producers, thereby enabling consumers to order fresh groceries and get them delivered at their home or office.

name: Good Uncle

The company partners with local chefs to prepare a food menu which keeps changing every 6 months, having a wide variety of cuisines which can be ordered and tracked using the company's mobile app, enabling subscribed customers to order meals online and get them delivered to their doorstep.

name: Goodmail Systems
description: Developer of email solutions. The company offers CertifiedEmail, which enables consumers to identify authentic email messages from legitimate commercial and nonprofit email senders as well as to identify email messages, which are real and sent from email senders with whom they have a pre-existing relationship.

name: Google
description: Alphabet is a holding company, with Google, the Internet media giant, as a wholly owned subsidiary. Google generates 99% of Alphabet revenue, of which more than 85% is from online ads. Google's other revenue is from sales of apps and content on Google Play and YouTube, as well as cloud service fees and other licensing revenue. Sales of hardware such as Chromebooks, the Pixel smartphone, and smart homes products, which include Nest and Google Home, also contribute to other revenue. Alphabet's moonshot investments are in its other bets segment, where it bets on technology to enhance health (Verily), faster Internet access to homes (Google Fiber), self-driving cars (Waymo), and more. Alphabet's operating margin has been 25%-30%, with Google at 30% and other bets operating at a loss.

name: Gooten
description: Developer of a drop-shipping e-commerce platform designed to revolutionize product fulfillment. The company's platform uses an international network of manufacturers with drop-shipping capabilities and handles manufacturing, delivery and also provides customer support, enabling businesses to get custom merchandise made, printed and shipped.

name: GPShopper

name: Grand Street

name: Grayce

name: Greats

name: GreenBorder Technologies
